How it runs

Four ways the plan works harder than its asset list

  • The format is the argument. One can alone makes the packshot answer 'a can looks cheap', with no extra claim needed.
  • Built for the open answers. Every asset has a bottle and a no-bottle variant, so the old-bottle answer changes a frame, not the idea.

Your brief

DRAFT · 5 slides need a person
Territories

Territory: The One Good Can

Treat a single can of Hollow Oak Still the way this audience treats one good bottle: chosen with care, carried to a friend's table and set down as the thing you brought.

Why it fits
This answers IC1 directly. They treat themselves to one good bottle rather than a bulk pack (brief:audience, req:R6), and this launch comes in a can (prompt:1, req:R1). The work shows the can on its own, chosen and placed, never stacked or multipacked. That answers the objection that a can looks cheap, and it puts the brand on the supper table rather than in the cider aisle (storyline reframe, brief:audience, req:R5).
Mood
Warm, close and domestic. One can on a laid table at Friday supper, with hands setting it down beside the bread and glasses. Natural evening light. Plenty of empty space around the packshot, so the can reads as singular. Sound is the room, not the drink: chairs, low talk, a plate going down. Nobody hands out packs, and nothing sits on ice.
Risks
["Category safety: the 'one good thing' framing must not make 'one' sound like a moderation or health message, since health and mood claims are held until R&D and legal confirm (brief:mandatories, req:R18).", "Ownability: canned wine or other premium cans could make the same 'single chosen can' gesture; stillness and the orchard have to be visible in the frame to keep it ours.", 'Open question for a person: does the old bottle appear beside the can (brief:mandatories, req:R22)? The route changes depending on the answer.', 'No research figures support the bottle-versus-can tension yet. IC1 is marked low confidence and needs testing with the audience.']

Bring one good thing. Hollow Oak Still, on purpose.

Illustrative, not final
21
DRAFT · 5 slides need a person
Territories

Territory: Nothing Happens

Make the absence of fizz the event: no hiss, no rising bubbles, no rush, and let the stillness itself be the news.

Why it fits
This answers IC2 and IC3. To this audience, cider has come to mean fizzy, sweet and heavy, so they order something else (brief:insight, req:R9). Of those words, only fizz can be answered today, and stillness is the one answer this product owns (brief:smp, req:R10, prompt:1). 'Still' carries the news and the word 'cider' steps back, so there is no argument about what the category means. The route says nothing about sweetness until R&D and legal confirm (req:R18).
Mood
Quiet and held. Long static frames, and a pour where the surface settles flat and stays flat. Key visuals use generous blank space with one small, precise line of type. Sound design is near-silence, so the can opening is deliberately undramatic. The palette is muted and natural, with no condensation drama and no splashes.
Risks
["Category safety: stillness must not tip into a mood or wellbeing claim ('calming', 'unwind'). Those are held by the mandatory (brief:mandatories, req:R18), and copy needs legal review.", 'Quiet work can be invisible in a pub or in busy media. It needs a strong, repeatable visual device to register.', "Ownability: 'still' is a product descriptor any still drink could use. We own it only while we are the first still orchard cider in a can (prompt:1, req:R1), which the team should confirm can be said.", "The brief's insight line is marked 'to confirm'. If research shows fizz is not the real barrier, the route loses its footing."]

No hiss. No rush. Still, on purpose.

Illustrative, not final
22
DRAFT · 5 slides need a person
Territories

Territory: Orchard Time

Let the orchard's slow calendar of seasons, waiting and old trees be the proof behind the can, so the drink is understood as something made at the orchard's pace.

Why it fits
This answers IC3's implication: let the orchard carry the proof rather than arguing for the word 'cider' (brief:insight, prompt:1). The orchard is a named brand asset alongside the new can (brief:mandatories, req:R21). The route gives the 'still' idea a source and a reason, and gives this audience something to tell a friend at the table that is not about fizz or weight (brief:audience).
Mood
Pastoral but modern, not heritage-nostalgic. Bark, branches, mist, frost and blossom, shot in close textures and wide quiet landscapes, with no fruit in frame. The can appears at the end, set on a table. Ambient outdoor sound such as wind in leaves and birds gives way to the hush of an indoor supper. Restrained, earthy palette and clean contemporary type.
Risks
['Apples must not be shown until legal explains why (brief:mandatories, req:R20). An orchard without apples is hard to read and needs careful art direction.', "Pastoral codes risk looking like the category's traditional look, and may speak more to the protected 55+ rural core than to the 25-40 lead audience (req:R7, req:R8). It needs a modern treatment.", "Ownability: provenance and orchard imagery are common across drinks, so the link to 'still' and the can must be explicit.", 'We must not claim process or ageing facts the inputs do not give. Any statement about how or how long the cider is made needs a person to supply and approve it.']

The orchard doesn't hurry. Neither does Hollow Oak Still.

Illustrative, not final

Territories

We recommend 'The One Good Can'

TerritoryWhy (or why not)
The One Good CanIt answers the insight directly by making the single chosen can the hero, it is specific to this launch and travels well from social to out-of-home to in-venue, though the ownability and bottle-or-no-bottle questions need resolving.
Nothing HappensStillness is a distinctive, ownable product truth that gives a clear visual and sonic device, but it is a little removed from the one-good-bottle insight and quiet work risks going unnoticed in busy media.
Orchard TimeThe orchard provenance is credible and gives the drink a story, but it is the least tied to the insight, leans on common pastoral codes, and is hampered by the no-apples constraint and the lack of supplied process facts.

Internal note: Chosen by: default: the judge's first choice, flagged for Gate 2. Ranked by: claude-sonnet-5-5.

How it runs

How we would run it with you

1

Put the open questions to the client: why no apples, whether the old bottle sits beside the can, and when R&D confirms the sugar story.

2

Test the one-good-bottle versus can tension with 25-40 drinkers who rarely drink cider, because it is low confidence and no research supports it yet.

3

Build the key visual first, then cut the size crops, packshot and storyboard frames from it so that one can stays the hero throughout.

4

Prepare a bottle and a no-bottle variant of the packshot and end frame until the client answers req:R22.

5

Legal reviews every line for health, mood and sugar claims and confirms the responsible drinking line. No competition is planned; if one is added, it needs legal terms and a no-purchase route.

6

Ask the client where the can is stocked at launch, since the work invites people to bring it to a friend's table and look for it in the pub.
